summary: BifrOSt has no app-facing API to create or run virtual machines. Developer-only QEMU/KVM scripts boot Arch and installer guests for testing the shell; apps and the desktop cannot reach them. Apple's macOS guest, Rosetta and iCloud-in-guest features have no BifrOSt counterpart.

features.note: Apple entitlement model does not apply; BifrOSt sandboxes apps with bubblewrap and has no VM grant

features.feature: Displaying a guest in a window
features.note: GuestView (core/src/guest_display.rs) places a guest picture in a view, maps view points to guest pixels and routes keys with click and release-key capture; these are tested headless in core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-05.rs. Still missing: it is not wired into apps or the shell, and no guest has been shown on the VM or Midget; tools/arch-vm-iso.sh opens QEMU in a Hyprland window, and the desktop has no embeddable guest view.

features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/guest_vm.rs (GraphicsDevice, Scanout, Device::Graphics, GuestConfig::validate, GuestConfig::graphics, GraphicsDevice::framebuffer_bytes); tools/arch-vm.sh uses virtio-gpu for the guest shell
features.note: GuestConfig can describe a graphics device with one to four scanouts of one to 8192 pixels per side (BifrOSt limits), and validate refuses a device with no scanout, too many, a bad size or a second device. Tests: a_graphics_device_with_one_display_is_valid, a_graphics_device_may_drive_up_to_the_scanout_limit, a_display_side_must_be_between_one_and_the_pixel_limit (springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-tests-10.rs). The framebuffer bytes of each scanout and the device lookup are tested headless in springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-06.rs. Nothing starts a guest from this model yet (that needs the hypervisor on the lab machine), and only the dev harness configures a virtio-gpu; not yet tested on Midget
